slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will make you
intellectually lethal

reading the classics

read 10 pages of a classic novel every night: tolstoy, austen, dostoevsky. old books train your attention and your vocabulary in a way that no summary ever will.

explaining it simply

after learning anything new, explain it out loud in three sentences as if to a child. if you can't, you don't understand it yet, and now you know exactly where to look.

chess puzzles

solve one chess puzzle a day, even as a complete beginner. thinking three moves ahead is a skill that quietly spreads into every conversation and decision you make.

one subject a month

pick one subject a month and spend 5 minutes a day on it: philosophy, astronomy, economics. a year later you can hold your own on twelve topics most people avoid.

pick one subject a month and spend 5 minutes a day on it: philosophy, astronomy. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, and a year later you know twelve new subjects.

slides.texte_overlay:
writing it down

end every day by writing down one thing you learned and one thing you still don't get. the questions you keep are worth just as much as the answers you find.
